newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Oil companies firm in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Oil companies firm in New York.

text.p: Foreign oil companies' American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) firmed Wednesday, bolstered by rising oil prices.
"Oils are doing the dead cat bounce here. That's the story of the day," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
He said the oil shares were recovering from recent selling in recent days. They also were helped by rising oil prices, with Brent North Sea crude up $0.41 a barrel at its intraday high in London.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co rose 3/4 to 170-1/4 and British Petroleum Co Plc was up 1-1/2 to 134-7/8. France's Total SA rose 1/8 to 41 and Spain's Repsol rose 3/8 to 42.

Swedish pharmaceutical company Astra AB fell one to 44-5/8, dragged down by ratings downgrades of its U.S. partner Merck & Co Inc. The cuts took place because of doctors' favorable reception for Warner-Lambert Co's competing anti-cholesterol drug Lipitor.
Among Latin American ADRs, Brazilian telephone company Telebras SA rose 1-7/8 to 116-3/8. Its volume was among the most active on the New York Stock Exchange.
The most active ADR, troubled Canadian gold mining company Bre-X Minerals, fell 10/32 to 1-11/16 amid continuing skepticism about its Indonesian gold find.
Advancers led decliners 238 to 192 among 806 ADRs. The ADR index rose 0.12 percent and volume was 26 million shares in late morning.
